references.text: This version of Jesus' love for the disciples is directly linked to the Father's giving of all things to the Son, a theme repeated in [ref:Joh 3:35|John 3:35], where it says that the Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hands.

Jesus' awareness of his origin and purpose—that he came from God and returns to God—is clearly expressed in [ref:Joh 16:28|John 16:28]: "I came from the Father and entered the world; now I am leaving the world again and going back to the Father."

The motif that Jesus completed what the Father gave him to do, and then returns to the Father to receive his glory, reflects [ref:Joh 17:4-5|John 17:4-5], where Jesus prays to be given the glory he had with the Father before the world existed.

Jesus' authority to lay down his life and take it up again, based on a command from the Father, highlights his awareness that all things have been given into his hands, as in [ref:Joh 10:18|John 10:18].
The moment when Jesus gives up his spirit and completes his work is the practical fulfillment of him "going to God", as described in [ref:Joh 19:30|John 19:30].
